question: How does component-wise token normalization change the full-versus-fixed-time transfer contrast?
primary_population: Complete 1167 clips, 30091 reference units, 20 source groups; reused assessment.
gain_definition: WER(full) - WER(fixed-time); positive favors fixed-time mixing.
interaction_definition: [normalized FC - normalized FT] - [native FC - native FT]
bootstrap: 10000 paired archived-source-group resamples; same indices for all four states.
interpretation: Component-wise normalization changes length weighting and relative objective contributions. It does not isolate a global learning-rate or gradient-norm mechanism.
